definitions.gloss: detour; dawdling; loitering on the way
definitions.explanation: Stopping or lingering along the way instead of going directly to one's destination. Often used with する or {食|く}う. Originally referred to a horse stopping to eat grass on the roadside.

examples.japanese: {道草|みちくさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|く}った→食う：02657_kuu⟧。
{子|こ}ども⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{道草|みちくさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{帰|かえ}り→帰り：01275_kaeri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遅|おそ}く→遅い：00533_osoi⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The child dawdled on the way and got home late.

examples.japanese: {道草|みちくさ}⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧⟦まっすぐ→まっすぐ：00866_massugu⟧⟦{帰|かえ}って→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧き⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly used in the set phrase {道草|みちくさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|く}う→食う：02657_kuu⟧ (to dawdle, literally "to eat roadside grass"). Can also be used with ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧. Typically describes children loitering on the way home from school, but applies to anyone making unnecessary stops.

ETYMOLOGY:
From ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ (road) + ⟦{草|くさ}→草：02206_kusa⟧ (grass). Originally described a horse stopping to graze on grass along the road during a journey, delaying the traveler.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道草|みちくさ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|く}う→食う：02657_kuu⟧ (to dawdle on the way)
- {道草|みちくさ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to loiter, to make detours)
